nodes.summary: The coercion of the norm of a cusp form is the norm of its coercion as a modular form.
nodes.title: Cusp form norm agrees with the modular form norm

nodes.summary: The norm trick: two modular forms satisfying a commutation relation under the slash action of `ℋ` give rise to a modular form `Φ` of level `ℋ` with `Φ * G = F * norm ℋ G`.
nodes.title: Norm trick for modular forms

nodes.summary: The index of `Γ₀(2)` in `SL(2, ℤ)` is 3: the cosets are classified by the first column mod 2, and there are three nonzero vectors in `(ZMod 2)²`.
nodes.title: Γ₀(2) has index 3 in SL(2, ℤ)

nodes.summary: The norm of a cusp form vanishes if and only if the form itself vanishes: the norm is a product of translates, and a translate of a nonzero form is nonzero.
nodes.title: Norm of a cusp form vanishes only for the zero form

nodes.summary: The product norm of a cusp form: for `𝒢` of finite relative index in `ℋ`, the product of the `ℋ / 𝒢`-translates of `f`, viewed as a cusp form on the larger group `ℋ` at weight `k * [ℋ : 𝒢]`. This lifts Mathlib's `ModularForm.norm` to cusp forms; the only new work is checking vanishing at the cusps, which follows because each translate is a cusp form.
nodes.title: Norm of a cusp form

nodes.summary: Every weight-two cusp form on `Γ₀(2)` is zero. Take the norm of `f` to `Γ₀(1)`: it has weight `2 * [Γ₀(1) : Γ₀(2)] = 6`, hence vanishes by the level-one dimension formula, and the norm vanishes only when `f` does.
nodes.title: No nonzero weight-two cusp forms on Γ₀(2)

nodes.summary: Every weight-two cusp form on `Γ₀(1)` is zero: `Γ₀(1)` is the full modular group, and the dimension formula gives rank zero below weight 12.
nodes.title: No nonzero weight-two cusp forms of level one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
